headline: A new Attach button failure drove 169 reports in one month, while Outlook.com sign-in stayed the worst-served pain at 12 percent resolved.
narrative_md:
One new problem explains almost all of this month's growth. Support questions rose from 977 to 1030. The attachments category jumped from 29 to 190. Behind that sits a single new cluster: the Attach button does nothing and the file picker never opens. It accounts for 169 questions, with an average severity of 4.0 out of 5. The suspected cause is a stale value in the mail.compose.attach.dir setting, which stores the last folder used for attachments. Bugs 2077526 and 2077590 track it.

Volume is not the only signal. Two older clusters serve users badly. Microsoft and Outlook.com OAuth2 failures (OAuth2 is a sign-in method that uses tokens instead of a password) resolve only 12 percent of the time. Half of those questions get no answer at all. Generic "cannot receive new mail" reports resolve 27 percent of the time, with 41 percent unanswered. Both carry high severity. Helpers appear to lack the information needed to diagnose them.

Some areas improved. Send and receive questions fell from 233 to 160. Account and login fell from 165 to 135. The AT&T certificate problem grew but resolves at 87 percent, so helpers have a working answer. Startup hangs and broken calendar add-ons also resolve well.

This signal comes from a language model reading free-text support questions. Treat it as a triage pointer, not proof.

issues.why: This cluster is new, it produced 169 questions in one month, and 161 of them scored severity 4 or higher.
issues.action: Engineering should consider looking at how mail.compose.attach.dir is read at compose time, and adding a fallback when the stored folder no longer exists.

issues.why: Gmail users report a mail problem that no one can diagnose, and only 34 percent of these questions reach a resolution.
issues.action: Engineering should consider adding a one-click diagnostic export that captures protocol logs and account settings for Gmail accounts.

issues.why: Mail simply stops arriving with no error shown, 41 percent of reports get no reply, and only 27 percent resolve.
issues.action: Engineering should consider surfacing fetch failures in the interface instead of failing silently, so users can report an actual error code.

issues.why: A revoked certificate on inbound.att.net blocked mail downloads for AT&T users, though helpers resolved 87 percent of cases.
issues.action: Engineering should consider a clearer certificate error dialog that names the server and the reason, and tracking provider certificate changes.

issues.why: Setup wizard failures over hostname, ports and credentials still produce 28 questions, and a quarter get no answer.
issues.action: Engineering should consider logging which autoconfiguration step failed and showing that step to the user in the wizard.

issues.why: Users move to a new computer and lose mail and address books, which is unrecoverable data loss from the user point of view.
issues.action: Engineering should consider a guided profile export and import flow that verifies the copy before the old machine is retired.

issues.why: Junk filter complaints more than doubled, from 8 to 19, although severity stays low at 2.4.
issues.action: Engineering should consider checking whether a recent change reset junk training data or altered the adaptive filter thresholds.

issues.why: This is the worst-served cluster in the data, with 12 percent resolved, 50 percent unanswered and severity 4.3.
issues.action: Engineering should consider reproducing Outlook.com OAuth2 token refresh against current Microsoft endpoints and publishing a known-good configuration.

issues.why: Startup hangs tied to session.json, message loading and profile locks remain high severity but resolve at 80 percent.
issues.action: Engineering should consider making a corrupt session.json recoverable at startup rather than requiring manual file deletion.

issues.why: CardBook, Provider for Google Calendar and TbSync broke after Thunderbird updates, nearly tripling reports from 5 to 14.
issues.action: Engineering should consider testing these three add-ons against release candidates and warning users before an update disables them.

issues.why: Questions about out-of-office replies, return receipts and reply prefixes grew to 23, and 22 percent get no answer.
issues.action: Engineering should consider whether these settings are hard to find, and grouping them in one place in the settings interface.

issues.why: Folders vanish from the folder pane after an update, severity averages 4.4, and only 43 percent of reports resolve.
issues.action: Engineering should consider checking whether update-time folder database rebuilds drop subscriptions or orphan local folder entries.
